notes: One refinement to the director's dedupe rule, straight from the next route line: a camera or viewpoint LoRA — POV, mirror shot, a particular angle — is its own concept, not a duplicate of the subject. The one-per-concept rule had the director picking only the subject LoRA, which stood the user's POV-composition LoRA down along with the genuine near-duplicates, on exactly the unusual-camera shots where composition help matters most. The director is now told to pick a framing LoRA alongside the subject pick whenever the shot's viewpoint matches one.
